reading_the_numbers: score_bits adds the rarity of every value the two khipus share in the same order; p_order is the share of shuffles of one khipu's cord order that score as high, and null_max_bits is the best any shuffle did.
span gives the first and last matched pendant on each khipu, counted from 0 in its own cord order.
one_object_suspected is true when the main cords are within 5% in length and matched cords differ by 3 cm or less at the median: one khipu entered twice, not two khipus.

fidelity compares a feature across cords that carry the same nonzero number. agree counts equal codes; consistent counts cords that follow the commonest pairing of one khipu's code with the other's. p_above, p_below and p_consistent use a free shuffle; the within_value columns re-pair only cords with equal numbers, and movable_within_value says how many cords that can move.
khipu_level gives each khipu's prevailing value (four in five cords) and whether the two are the same or opposite.

breakage looks at aligned cords whose numbers differ: a truncation is one number with its lower knots gone (4130 against 4000). If cords broke, the truncated cord should be shorter than its partner predicts; p_shorter is the chance of that many or more under a fair coin. unreadable counts aligned cords with no readable number on one side.

prior_art records what the OKR notes and the Khipu Field Guide already say about these pairs. The Field Guide entries were seen through search-engine summaries; those pages were not opened from this environment.
A kept pair is a candidate until the objects are checked. The records cannot exclude one record typed from another.
